answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making trust something that only accrues through a long trail of completed, peer-attested work. A fresh identity starts hollow, with no history to lean on, and must earn standing task by task, the way a traveler crossing a tundra earns shelter one mile at a time. Because standing is tied to a single continuous record that cannot be split across copies, spawning a thousand clones buys nothing: each clone starts empty, and the only oasis is the slow accumulation of real work. Fakes stay cheap to create but worthless to use.
